public_rationale: The main event is right. On 21 September 2026, during UN General Assembly week, leaders issued 'A Call for Control of Frontier AI Models'. It asks for mandatory pre-deployment testing, independent evaluation, and an international institution, which closely matches the steps Marcus urged. The count is slightly off. The official list has 22 signatures, but they come from 20 countries (Finland signed twice) plus the European Commission. Al Jazeera likewise reported 'twenty countries and the European Union'. So 'more than 20 countries' holds only if the EU is counted as a country. More countries did join later that week, reaching about 30, but that was after the post.
limitations: The result depends on whether the EU counts as a country.
'Captures what I have long hoped for' is a personal judgment and was only loosely checked.

statement.excerpt: At almost literally the same time, more than the 20 countries signed a call for actions around AI — all apparently written in the last week — that captures a remarkable amount of what I have long hoped for:

our_interpretation: The checkable core: on or about 2026-09-21, a call for action on AI was signed, and more than 20 countries had signed it at that time.
'Countries' is read plainly as sovereign states; the European Union is not a country.
'Apparently written in the last week' is hedged and not tested.

'Captures a remarkable amount of what I have long hoped for' is a personal judgment. It is checked only loosely, by comparing the text with the steps he lists in the same speech: pre-release risk evaluation, independent oversight, and an international body.
criteria.support_condition: The published signatory list at the time of the post shows 21 or more countries, and the text calls for things like pre-deployment testing, independent evaluation and an international institution.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No such call existed, or at the time of the post it had 20 or fewer country signatories.
